z2m.title: Zigbee2MQTT
z2m.description: Hive Local looks up your Hive receivers in Zigbee2MQTT. Change the base topic only if you've changed it in Zigbee2MQTT.

device.title: Choose receiver
device.description: These are the Hive receivers Zigbee2MQTT knows about. Hot water is offered automatically on receivers that have it.

zha.title: Choose receiver
zha.description: Pick the Hive receiver (SLR1, SLR2 or OTR1) from your ZHA devices. Hot water is offered automatically on receivers that have it.

error.no_bridge: Zigbee2MQTT didn't send its device list. Check that MQTT is set up, Zigbee2MQTT is running, and the base topic is right.
error.no_receivers: Zigbee2MQTT has no Hive receivers that aren't already added.
error.not_hive: That device has no Thermostat cluster, or ZHA hasn't finished loading it. Pick the receiver (SLR or OTR), not the wall thermostat.

abort.no_zha: ZHA isn't set up in Home Assistant.

receiver_silent.title: {name} isn't responding
receiver_silent.description:
Hive Local hasn't heard from the receiver **{name}** for over 30 minutes, even when asking it for its state. Check that it has power and that Zigbee2MQTT or ZHA can reach it (its light should be steady, not flashing). Its schedule keeps running on the receiver itself, but Home Assistant can't change it or show its state until it's back.

This goes away by itself once the receiver reports again.

z2m_no_state.title: {name} hasn't reported through Zigbee2MQTT
z2m_no_state.description:
Hive Local asked for the state of **{name}** on the MQTT topic `{topic}` and got nothing back in 5 minutes. This almost always means the receiver was renamed in Zigbee2MQTT, or Zigbee2MQTT's base topic changed. Check the receiver's friendly name and the base topic in Zigbee2MQTT; if either changed, remove this receiver from Hive Local and add it again.

This goes away by itself once the receiver reports.

confirm.title: Reload {name}
confirm.description:
Hive Local can't find the receiver **{name}** in ZHA. ZHA may still be starting or reloading, or the receiver was removed from ZHA. Hive Local reconnects by itself when ZHA has it again.

Reload Hive Local's entry for **{name}** now, so it looks the receiver up in ZHA again?

thermostat_quiet.title: {name} has gone quiet
thermostat_quiet.description:
The Hive thermostat **{name}** hasn't reported a temperature for a while. The receiver drops a thermostat it doesn't hear from, shows a red light and "No signal", and turns the boiler off. Check the thermostat's batteries and that it's in range of a Zigbee router. Hive Local asks it to report every 2 minutes once it's awake.

This goes away by itself once the thermostat reports again.

valve_battery_low.title: {name}'s battery is low
valve_battery_low.description:
The Hive radiator valve **{name}** (`{entity_id}`) reports {battery}% battery. Replace its batteries soon: when they run out it stops responding and the radiator stays as it is.

This goes away by itself once the battery reads higher.

valve_unavailable.title: {name} isn't responding
valve_unavailable.description:
The Hive radiator valve **{name}** (`{entity_id}`) has been unavailable in Home Assistant for over 30 minutes. Check its batteries and that it's in range of a Zigbee router. Its room can't be controlled through it until it's back.

This goes away by itself once the valve responds again.
